full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 2, 2026 2:26pm Morgan Wallen performs onstage for the 16th Annual Darius and Friends St. Jude Benefit at Ryman Auditorium on June 2, 2025, in Nashville, Tennessee. Jason Kempin/Getty Images for ABA Morgan Wallen ‘s I’m the Problem is back on top of Billboard ‘s albums chart, the publication reported on Sunday, more than a year after the country star first released the project in May 2025, and over seven months since the album last reached number one back in January. I’m the Problem managed to best both Olivia Rodrigo ‘s eight-week-old You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love and Charli XCX ‘s brand new Music , Fashion, Film in one of the tightest chart races of the year so far. Wallen earned 80,000 units this week, while Rodrigo’s LP, which topped the charts for two weeks this summer, came in with just under 80,000 units. Charli’s Brat follow-up, meanwhile, opened with 78,000 units. Related Stories Music Ariana Grande to "Step Back From Visibility" After Tour Ends Amid "Ongoing Public Scrutiny" Music K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure While I’m the Problem hasn’t hit No. 1 since January, it’s been a chart monster overall, staying in the top 10 since its release over a year ago. It’s one of two top 10 albums for Wallen, with his 2023 album One Thing at a Time clocking in at seven this week. I’m the Problem has spent 63 weeks on the Billboard albums chart, while One Thing at a Time has racked 178 weeks. Wallen’s number one return comes as the singer released his latest song, “Been by Now,” last Friday. The question now becomes where that song will land on Monday’s new Hot 100 chart. Through all his controversies, Wallen remains the biggest streaming act in a country boom that’s also propelled the likes of Zach Bryan, Luke Combs and Ella Langley, the latter of whom currently has three songs in the top 10 on the Hot 100, including song of the summer contender “Choosin’ Texas.” For Rodrigo, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love has logged its fifth consecutive week at number two after spending its first two weeks atop the chart. For Charli, Music, Fashion, Film opens with a similar debut to Brat, which debuted with 77,000 units back in 2024. THR

title: Ariana Grande to “Step Back From Visibility” After Tour Ends Amid “Ongoing Public Scrutiny”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 2, 2026 1:12pm Ariana Grande Monica Schipper/Getty Images Ariana Grande is planning to take a step back from the public eye after the Eternal Sunshine Tour wraps, including dropping out of Sunday in the Park with George . This decision comes after the Grammy-winning singer has faced a wave of online commentary surrounding her health and body over the last year. Most recently, discussions intensified after the release of her new music video for her song “Petal,” with many fans pointing out her noticeably thinner appearance in the footage. “Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour,” her rep shared in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Sunday. Her tour concludes on Sept. 1 after her 10-show residency in London. Related Stories Music K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure Music Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Have the Longest-Running No. 1 in U.K. History “She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” the rep added. “This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.” Grande has been booked and busy the last few years , filming Wicked and Wicked: For Good , which released in 2024 and 2025, respectively. She had also been campaigning for awards for both films, ultimately earning a best supporting actress Oscar nomination for her role as Glinda in the first film. On the music side, she dropped her seventh studio album, Eternal Sunshine , in 2024, before heading out on a 3-month-long tour starting in June. She also just released her eighth studio album, Petal , at the end of July. A source close to the singer also told THR that her new album is “a fight song.” They added that it’s an “anthem about the love-hate relationship with the public and their toxicity. This album is not about any romantic partner or breakup in that way.” Grande next stars in Focker-in-Law , opposite Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller, which hits theaters on Nov. 25. It’s unclear if Grande plans to participate in the film’s upcoming press tour. The “hate that i made you love me” singer was also set to appear, opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey, in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George . However, THR confirmed Grande will no longer be participating in the project, which opens at London’s Barbican Centre next summer. The production will cast another lead to replace Grande. “Following this evening’s announcement from Ariana Grande’s team, we can confirm that she has decided to step back from Sunday in the Park with George ,” Empire Street Productions shared in a statement. “We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support. The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course.” People was first to report the news of Grande stepping back from visibility after the tour. Caitlin Huston contributed to this report. THR

title: Nancy Guthrie Case Haunted by Sheriff’s Department’s Possible Mistakes
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 2, 2026 11:20am Pima County Sheriff, Chris Nanos, speaks to the media on Feb. 3, 2026, in Tucson, Arizona. Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images As the investigation into Nancy Guthrie ‘s kidnapping case crosses the six-month mark, a new report from The Wall Street Journal is highlighting possible mistakes by the sheriff and lead investigators. The Pima County Sheriff’s Department, led by Chris Nanos, has been overseeing the investigation after Savannah Guthrie ‘s mom was reported missing on Feb. 1. As of Aug. 2, Nancy hasn’t been found and there have been no arrests in the case. After reviewing personnel files obtained in public records requests and conducting interviews with current and former county and federal officials and people close to the case, the WSJ has found that there were concerns from the start of the investigation, including who Nanos appointed head of homicide, Sgt. David Stivers. Related Stories TV Savannah Guthrie Issues Emotional Plea for Answers in Mom Nancy's Disappearance After Release of Ransom Notes TV Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie Case Releases Ransom Notes: "She Perished Shortly After She Was Taken" According to personnel records, Stivers was reprimanded two months before Nancy was kidnapped for “poor judgment,” as he was blamed for delays securing crime -scene evidence in a homicide case. The charges in that case were ultimately dropped for insufficient evidence, The Journal reported. When it came to Nancy’s case, people familiar with the investigation said Stivers and his detectives ignored the dried blood on her front porch for hours after they arrived on Feb. 1, suspecting that the blood came from some unrelated cause. “They failed to seal off the property with police tape to protect sensitive crime-scene evidence, allowing reporters, livestreamers, and Amazon and pizza delivery drivers entry to the porch,” the WSJ wrote. After undergoing DNA analysis, the blood samples were later confirmed to be Nancy’s. It’s now believed to be connected to her kidnapping. The WSJ later reported that Nanos promoted Stivers to lieutenant in July. The new role will reportedly take effect in September. Lt. Heather Lappin — Nanos’ opponent in the November 2024 election, where he was running for reelection (he ultimately won after a recount) — told The Hollywood Reporter in February that Nanos had removed some of the department’s best detectives because they supported her election campaign. “A lot of the Guthrie case is just consequences of his really bad decision-making, the years of decimating his units,” she told THR at the time. “Three of our best homicide detectives, probably in [all of] southern Arizona, were removed from Homicide because they supported me [in the election].” People familiar with the matter also told the Journal that Nanos put Lappin on administrative leave weeks before Election Day and sidelined deputies who had supported Lappin after being reelected. The department’s senior pilot, who had backed Nanos’ challenger in the election, was also demoted to patrol duty days before Nancy’s kidnapping following a workplace complaint. This led to more delays in the investigation on Feb. 1, as the department struggled for hours to find a flight deputy to operate its search-and-rescue plane, a $1.7 million Cessna surveillance aircraft, equipped with both infrared and zoom-lens cameras. Flight data reviewed by The Journal showed that by the time the plane got up in the air to begin its search, it was getting too dark to use its zoom-lens cameras. The WSJ said that Nanos has disputed its findings. “I can assure everybody that we are working hard every day with all of our partners,” the sheriff said, including “corporate America,” which has “offered up some assistance with some of the brightest minds in this country.” He added, “This case is not cold.” THR has also reached out to the Pima County Sheriff’s Department for comment. In addition to coming under fire from his own department, as Nanos was accused in March of hiding an extensive disciplinary record , the sheriff has also been criticized by Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel. Neither Nanos and Patel has announced any further breaks in Nancy’s case, despite the latter also promising early on to lead the charge on the federal side. In May, during an interview on Sean Hannity’s Hang Out with Sean Hannity podcast, Patel accused Nanos of sidelining FBI agents early in the investigation. “For four days, we were kept out of the investigation,” he said. The sheriff pushed back against those claims in an interview, stating that there weren’t any delays. If Patel “really believes that we tried to block them or keep them out of this or not share things,” Nanos said, “I, 100 percent, want him to call me because that’s the furthest from the truth.” According to The Journal , Nanos said he has never spoken to Patel. Throughout the case, Savannah has continued to take to social media , pleading for answers in her mom’s disappearance. On Saturday, after Nanos released a pair of ransom notes initially sent to the CBS affiliate in her home city of Tucson, Arizona, the Today co-anchor asked that anyone with information come forward. “We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward,” Savannah wrote on Instagram. “Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes. Someone has noticed something different, strange, troubling or just unusual — perhaps with someone they deeply love. Perhaps they are afraid to come forward. Perhaps they are conflicted. Perhaps they are angry or upset for being in this situation. There is a way out — to tell what you know. You can do so anonymously. The reward is available.” The Pima County Sheriff’s Department said the notes “purport to have been written by kidnappers.” The second note, which was sent to the CBS affiliate on Feb. 6, stated that Nancy “perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now.” Authorities said they decided to share the ransom notes publicly in hopes that someone recognizes “distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax and phraseology that reflect the writer’s unique linguistic style.” THR

title: Sally Field Won Her First Emmy for 1976’s ‘Sybil’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All August 2, 2026 11:00am Sally Field (left) as Sybil and Joanne Woodward as Dr. Cornelia Wilbur in Sybil, the NBC TV movie that gave Field the first of three Emmys. “The televised novel has hit a new plateau,” wrote THR’s Richard Hack. NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal/Getty Images Sally Field boasts a trio of Emmys. With her nominated performance as Tova Sullivan in the Netflix adaptation of Shelby Van Pelt’s Remarkably Bright Creatures — you know, “the octopus book” — she could easily snag a fourth. But statuettes are a lot like being smitten: You never forget your first time. For Field, that came courtesy of 1976’s Sybil . Not yet 30, the actress transformed herself from goofy TV sweetheart ( Gidget, The Flying Nun ) into a serious and layered performer by playing a woman suffering from dissociative identity disorder — and the 16 multiple personalities that came with her diagnosis. Related Stories TV Charlie Hunnam Adopted Kittens While Filming 'Monster' to Decompress From "Darkest Realm" of Playing Ed Gein TV How Rufus Sewell Found a TV Role Worth Staying For Reviewing the telepic at the time, THR ‘s Richard Hack wrote that Field “dominates the screen, switching from personality to personality like a sparrow hopping from branch to branch in a maple.” In the end, the two-night NBC special received a total of four Emmys and a nomination for Joanne Woodward, who played the title character’s psychiatrist. The impact on Field’s career was immediate. She’d be seen on the big screen, riding shotgun with Burt Reynolds in Smokey and the Bandit within a year of Sybil premiering. (Field has since won two Oscars, for Norma Rae and Places in the Heart .) But Sybil ‘s true legacy may be in how it shifted the face of a misunderstood diagnosis from Norman Bates doing mommy cosplay in Psycho to a young actress who was and remains one of the most likable (really!) women in Hollywood. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, who stars as the titular super-powered actor Simon Williams, said in a statement that he’s “glad we got to be a part of something cool” as he thanked fans for their “genuine love” they’ve shared over the show, which has earned him an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series. “Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back for Season 2,” he wrote on Instagram. “(And if you don’t knowww, now ya knoww!) title: Christopher Nolan Calls Out “A Real Problem” In Amateur Film Criticism

Aalok Soni/Getty Images for Universal Pictures With Letterboxd at the palm of our hands, everybody truly is a critic these days, much to Christopher Nolan ‘s annoyance. The 2x Oscar winner recently unpacked “a real problem” with amateur film critics today, explaining there is a “very accessible modern language of storytelling” that they don’t see as necessary to filmmaking. “The criticism that’s often leveled at movies in general is, ‘Oh, the character has to be made sympathetic, so the character is manipulated in different ways or changed in different ways,'” he told Beijing, China podcast host Zhong Shu . “And that’s a fundamental flaw of film criticism in a way, or storytelling criticism. Because to be able to identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism. And that’s a real problem in criticism today.” Related Stories Culture Joyce Carol Oates Defends Christopher Nolan & 'The Odyssey' Against Emily Wilson, Other Critics News Greek Prime Minister Congratulates Christopher Nolan On 'The Odyssey' Nolan continued, “Because people have this idea that, ‘Because I can understand why the story affects me the way it is, therefore, it didn’t work.’ That’s not how storytelling works. So, when we create a heroic figure in a story, as storytellers, we have to be mindful of the energy that the audience brings to that story and the interaction between our intention and the way the audience receives that. And the fact that that mechanism is identifiable to people doesn’t invalidate it.” Watch on Deadline With his latest film The Odyssey following that storytelling format through Homer’s ancient epic, to the tune of nearly $1B and counting, Nolan explained that amateur film critics need “to understand the necessity for the mechanisms.” Here is my interview with Christopher Nolan: are you a bard for a civilization at dusk? pic.twitter.com/dQION5v6bl — Yiyang Zhuge (@ZhugeYY) July 31, 2026 “So, you’re looking at a lingua franca of storytelling created by Hollywood for the last hundred years that is effectively universal. And so, it is its own language, and that language is understood by people all over the world, which is what’s incredible about it,” added Nolan. “And it is a very, very accessible modern language of storytelling, and it has certain rules, it has conventions. You can break those conventions. You can bend them. You can move them. But you have to be aware of them the whole time. “I’m thinking more of amateur criticism, because they feel they’ve identified the mechanism, they feel that it invalidates it. That can be true of certain elements, and film grammar, film language evolves with that. So when a trope becomes too familiar to an audience, then it has to be changed. But we do, as filmmakers, avail ourselves of that common language. We build on that understanding. Our audience has seen many films and they understand that language,” he said. Despite a lively online discourse around Nolan’s latest, The Odyssey currently holds a solid 94% critic rating and a 97% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. The Odyssey follows Odysseus (Matt Damon) through the incredible trials and mythical encounters he faces on his decade-long journey home to wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) after the Trojan War. The film also stars Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong’o, Jon Bernthal, Benny Safdie, John Leguizamo, Elliot Page, Himesh Patel, Bill Irwin, Samantha Morton, Jesse Garcia, Will Yun Lee, Rafi Gavron, Shiloh Fernandez, Mia Goth, Travis Scott and more.
